scenarios.title: A Kind Word From {tyler}
scenarios.text: {tyler} sends a message after a rough week, and it's kinder than you expected.

choices.label: Call him back
choices.result: You call him back. You talk for an hour, like old teammates.

choices.label: Reply with thanks
choices.result: You reply with thanks and one honest line about the week.

choices.label: Read it twice
choices.result: You read it twice and keep it.

scenarios.title: The Player Rep Meeting
scenarios.text: The players' union holds a meeting about health care for retired players.

choices.label: Speak at the meeting
choices.result: You speak for the players who aren't in the room anymore.

choices.label: Learn the details
choices.result: You learn the details and explain them to the young players.

choices.label: Read the summary
choices.result: You read the summary later. It's three pages, and most of it is about people you used to play with.

scenarios.title: The Players' Vote
scenarios.text: The team votes on a players-only issue, and they want you to speak first.

choices.label: Speak first
choices.result: You speak first, short and fair. The vote goes the way you hoped.

choices.label: Lay out both sides
choices.result: You lay out both sides and let them decide.

choices.label: Ask the young players
choices.result: You ask the young players to speak first. They do.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Crisis
scenarios.text: A rookie in crisis calls you at 2 a.m.

choices.label: Go to him
choices.result: You get dressed and go. You sit with him until the sun comes up.

choices.label: Call for help
choices.result: You stay on the phone and call the team's counselor. They're there in twenty minutes.

choices.label: Talk him through it
choices.result: You talk him through it on the phone, and you check on him every day after.

scenarios.title: The Second Business
scenarios.text: You consider a second business, while the first is still finding its feet.

choices.label: Wait a year
choices.result: You wait a year until the first one is steady.

choices.label: Do both
choices.result: You do both. You don't sleep much.

choices.label: Ask your partner in the first one
choices.result: You ask your partner. The answer is 'please not yet'.

scenarios.title: The Real Estate Pitch
scenarios.text: A real estate agent with very white teeth pitches you on rental properties. The numbers look great on her tablet.

choices.label: Study the numbers
choices.result: You take the numbers home, study them for a week and buy one small building. It's work, and it's yours.

choices.label: Ask {parent}
choices.result: You ask {parent}, who has strong opinions about landlords and stronger ones about leaky roofs. You don't buy, and you learn a lot.

choices.label: Pass on it
choices.result: You pass. You'd rather not fix anyone's sink, and the agent finds a linebacker by the end of the week.

scenarios.title: The Investment That Works
scenarios.text: An investment you made years ago, mostly to stop your advisor asking, has quietly turned into real money. Nobody knows about it but you.

choices.label: Leave it alone
choices.result: You leave it alone and let it keep growing. It's the first time money has felt like a plan instead of a pressure.

choices.label: Share some of it
choices.result: You use some of it to clear a family debt nobody talks about. The call where you tell them is short, and nobody can speak at the end.

choices.label: Treat yourself once
choices.result: You treat yourself once, quietly: the watch you looked at for years. You wear it on game days and feel a little foolish and very happy.

scenarios.title: The Tax Audit
scenarios.text: You're audited, and every receipt from the last three years matters.

choices.label: Hire an accountant
choices.result: You hire a good accountant. It's expensive and calm.

choices.label: Do it yourself
choices.result: You do it yourself, every night for a month. You learn a lot.

choices.label: Ask {love_interest} to help
choices.result: You and {love_interest} sort receipts at the kitchen table for a week.

scenarios.title: The Charity Scam
scenarios.text: A charity using your name turns out to be a scam.

choices.label: Go to the authorities
choices.result: You go to the authorities and make it public.

choices.label: Make it right
choices.result: You donate to the families who were fooled.

choices.label: Let your lawyer handle it
choices.result: You let your lawyer handle it. It takes a year, and the story keeps your name in it the whole time.

scenarios.title: The Bad Sponsor
scenarios.text: A sponsor is in the news for the wrong reasons, and your face is on its ads.

choices.label: End the deal
choices.result: You end the deal the same day and say why.

choices.label: Talk to the sponsor first
choices.result: You talk to the sponsor first. They pull the ads.

choices.label: Ride it out
choices.result: You ride it out. It costs you some fans.

scenarios.title: The Public Speaking Gig
scenarios.text: A company wants you to give a motivational talk to its employees.

choices.label: Give a real talk
choices.result: You give a real talk about failing and staying. They stand up.

choices.label: Tell stories
choices.result: You tell stories and laugh with them.

choices.label: Pass
choices.result: You pass. You're not a speaker.

scenarios.title: The Kids' Book
scenarios.text: A publisher wants you to write a children's book about learning to kick. The editor says to write it the way you'd tell it to a seven-year-old.

choices.label: Write it
choices.result: You write it at the kitchen table with your kids correcting every page. The dedication is to them, and they read it to their classes.

choices.label: Write it with {holder}
choices.result: You write it with {holder}, who insists on a chapter about the holder. It's funnier than the one you'd have written alone.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.result: You pass for now and tell the editor maybe after football. You keep the email, and some nights you start a first line in your head.

scenarios.title: The Commercial Shoot
scenarios.text: A national commercial shoot, and the director wants you to act.

choices.label: Go for it
choices.result: You go for it. The commercial is silly and everywhere.

choices.label: Keep it simple
choices.result: You ask for fewer lines. It works better.

choices.label: Do one take
choices.result: You do one take and leave. The director uses it, and it's stiff.
